Run one or more NONMEM models

Source: R/nm_run.R
nm_run.Rd

Sequentially launches a list of NONMEM control streams via the nmfe executable (direct call, no Wings for NONMEM, no PsN required). By default each run gets its own subdirectory <run>.reg inside analysis_dir, holding a copy of the control stream and all NONMEM output files; with run_subdir = "" the run is made directly in the folder of its control stream, as when nmfe is called by hand. The data file is not copied. A relative $DATA path is accepted: it is looked up from the folder of the control stream ($DATA data.csv), then from the run directory ($DATA ../data.csv, Wings style), and written as an absolute path in the copied control stream.

Usage

nm_run(
  ctl,
  nmfe_path,
  analysis_dir,
  skip_terminated = TRUE,
  accept_failed = TRUE,
  overwrite_ctl = TRUE,
  run_subdir = ".reg",
  verbose = TRUE,
  n_cores = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

ctl

Character vector of paths to .ctl files. May be absolute paths or file names relative to analysis_dir. (Formerly ctl_files, still accepted with a warning; the former order, nmfe_path first, is also recognised.)

nmfe_path

Full path to the nmfe executable (e.g. "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat" on Windows, "/opt/nm760/run/nmfe76" on Linux or macOS, where it is run directly and must be executable).

analysis_dir

Root directory of the analysis. One run subdirectory is created here for each run (see run_subdir). A warning is issued when it lies in a folder synchronised by a cloud client (Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud, Box): the client can lock the files written by NM-TRAN and make a run fail (silence it with options(nmpilot.warn_synced = FALSE)).

skip_terminated

Logical. If TRUE (default), runs whose .lst file already exists and reports a terminal state are skipped.

accept_failed

Logical. Only used when skip_terminated = TRUE. If TRUE (default), runs that terminated with an error are also skipped (not re-launched). If FALSE, only runs with run_ok = TRUE are skipped.

overwrite_ctl

Logical. If TRUE (default), the .ctl file is overwritten in the .reg directory if already present.

run_subdir

Suffix of the run subdirectories: ".reg" (default, Wings-compatible layout run001.reg/), any other suffix (e.g. ".run"), or "" to run in the folder of the control stream itself, without copying it (outputs next to the .ctl). Control streams in Wings label syntax need a subdirectory, because the converted copy is written there.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), progress messages are printed to the console.

n_cores

Number of runs launched at the same time (default 1: one after the other, NONMEM output shown in the console). A whole number, "auto" (physical cores minus one, see nm_cores()) or "ask" (interactive sessions: the cores are shown and the number is asked once per R session, then reused; options(nmpilot.n_cores = NULL) asks again). In parallel, each run is started in the background from its run directory; the console output of nmfe goes to <run>_nmpilot.log. Runs written in the same folder (run_subdir = "") are always run one after the other. If R is interrupted, the runs already started go on in the background.

...

Former argument names, accepted with a warning until version 1.0: ctl_files (now ctl).

Value

A run log of class nm_run_log (a data.frame, printed as a short summary), with one row per run and the following columns:

run

Run name (without extension).

reg_dir

Full path to the run directory (<run>.reg, or the folder of the control stream when run_subdir = "").

action

One of "launched", "skipped_done", or "skipped_no_ctl".

exit_status

Shell return code from nmfe (0 = success).

lst_exists

Logical: does the .lst file exist after the run?

ofv

Objective function value (OFV).

minimization_status

Minimization status string: "successful", "terminated", "rounding_errors", "min_success_cov_failed", "evaluation" (run without minimization, MAXEVAL=0; min_ok is then NA and run_ok TRUE), "simulation" (simulation-only run, $SIMULATION ONLYSIM, finished; ofv and min_ok are then NA and run_ok TRUE), or "unknown".

min_ok

Logical: did minimization succeed?

cov_ok

Logical: did the covariance step succeed?

run_ok

Logical: is the run globally acceptable (minimization and covariance both successful)?

cov_status

Detailed covariance step status: "successful", "aborted", "not_requested", or "unknown".

Details

Wings for NONMEM is not needed. The default .reg layout mirrors the Wings output structure (a run named run001.ctl produces a directory run001.reg/ containing run001.ctl, run001.lst, run001.ext, etc.), so that projects started with Wings can be continued; the other functions of the package read runs in any of these layouts.

Run status is parsed from the .lst file after completion. The skip_terminated mechanism reads any existing .lst before launching, allowing safe re-use of nm_run() on a partially completed batch.

See also

nm_extract_runs() for parsing NONMEM output files after a run.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
log <- nm_run(
  ctl             = c("run001.ctl", "run002.ctl", "run003.ctl"),
  nmfe_path       = "C:/nm76g64/run/nmfe76.bat",
  analysis_dir    = "C:/analyses/my_pk_project",
  skip_terminated = TRUE,
  accept_failed   = TRUE,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

# Show only failed runs
log[!log$run_ok, ]
} # }
